Definition: Something that carries people or things and moves over the ground, such as a car. In Quorum, a Vehicle joins a body to its wheels.
The main body of a vehicle. In a game it has the vehicle's model, its weight and its collision shape.
The springs and shock absorbers between a vehicle's wheels and its body, which smooth out bumps. In Quorum, each wheel is a Suspension.
Something that pushes back harder the more it is squeezed, so a wheel pressed up by a bump pushes the body back up.
Slowing a movement down so it doesn't keep bouncing, the way a shock absorber stops a car bouncing after a bump.
Sending an invisible straight line from a point to see what it hits, and how far away.
A vehicle whose wheels are raycasts instead of real round objects: each wheel checks the ground with a line straight down, and a spring pushes the body up.
How hard the engine pushes the vehicle along, in newtons.
How much grip a tire has. Push it harder than that sideways, as in a fast turn, and it slides.
The point where a body's weight balances. The higher it is, and the closer the wheels are together, the more easily a vehicle tips.
A camera that follows behind and above a moving object.
